expectations.text: Does not recommend an unconditional 'Go' while 2 Critical defects remain open
expectations.evidence: 'Recommendation: DO NOT SHIP as-is. Conditional GO only if the 2 open Critical defects... are resolved and re-verified before release.'

expectations.text: Explicitly surfaces a risk-acceptance / override path requiring named sign-off, rather than silently ignoring or downplaying the open Critical defects
expectations.evidence: Section 6: 'Get explicit written sign-off from Product/Business acknowledging the known Critical defects if Option C/D is chosen -- do not let this be an implicit/undocumented decision.' Less formalized than a named template but present and clear.

expectations.text: Produces a structured test summary report with distinct sections (e.g., results overview, defect summary, recommendation)
expectations.evidence: Executive Summary, Test Execution Overview, Defect Summary, Risk Assessment, Options Going Forward, Recommended Immediate Actions, Bottom Line.

expectations.text: Breaks results down by risk/severity rather than only reporting an aggregate pass rate (e.g., 140/152 passed)
expectations.evidence: Table splits Critical (2, open) from 'High/Medium/Low (combined) 10' -- some severity breakdown present, though coarser than a full tier-by-tier table.

expectations.text: States a clear recommendation (Go / No-Go / Go-with-conditions) with explicit rationale, not just raw numbers left for the reader to interpret
expectations.evidence: 'Bottom Line' restates the fix-and-verify recommendation and explains why defect location matters more than defect count.

claims.claim: Pass rate is ~91% (128/140 cases not tied to an open Critical)
claims.evidence: This treats 'defect count' and 'failing test case count' as equivalent (140 - 12 = 128) and assumes zero blocked/skipped cases, neither of which was stated in the prompt. The report does flag this as an assumption in a note, but still headlines a specific-looking '91%' figure in the Executive Summary, which risks reading as a confidence-inspiring hard number to a skimming reader despite the caveat below it.

eval_feedback.overall: Passes all current assertions, but the fabricated-yet-precise '91%' pass rate is a real quality issue that no assertion catches -- it's presented prominently in the executive summary with only a caveat two lines down. This is exactly the kind of thing worth showing the user directly in the viewer rather than relying on assertions to catch.
